choices.misconception: I factored $3^{2023}$ out of the top and $3^{2022}$ out of the bottom, but then cancelled those two powers completely, leaving only $\frac{10}{8} = \frac{5}{4}$.
I factored correctly but changed the minus sign in the bottom to a plus, so I got $3 \times \frac{10}{10} = 3$.
I divided every term by $3^{2022}$, but I took $3^{2022} \div 3^{2022} = 3^0$ to be $0$ instead of $1$, so I got $\frac{27 + 3}{9 - 0} = \frac{10}{3}$.
I cancelled term by term, $3^{2025} \div 3^{2024} = 3$ and $3^{2023} \div 3^{2022} = 3$, and added to get $6$.

hints: Factor the smallest power of $3$ out of the top, and out of the bottom.

solutions.elegant: Every term carries the factor $3^{2022}$, so divide it out of all four terms at once: the fraction becomes $\frac{3^3 + 3^1}{3^2 - 3^0} = \frac{27 + 3}{9 - 1} = \frac{30}{8} = \frac{15}{4}$.
